newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Kia denies rejecting creditors' demands.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Kia denies rejecting creditors' demands.

text.p: South Korea's troubled Kia Group denied a local television report on Thursday that it had decided to reject demands by creditor banks, including a call for the unconditional resignation of group executives.
"No decision has yet been made on the demands," Kia's spokesman Jeun Sang-jin told Reuters by telephone.
Yonhap Television News said Kia had also decided to reject a demand that the group sell off its unit Asia Motors Corp.
Wednesday's meeting of Kia Group creditors failed to produce results after they determined that the group's self-rescue plans were insufficient.
Instead, they demanded Kia chairman Kim Sun-hong and other group executives promise to resign without condition and Asia Motors be sold off.
Kia had said it planned to sell part of Asia Motors' assets and let its flagship Kia Motors Corp absorb Asia Motors' core manufacturing lines.
The creditor banks are due to meet again on Friday to detail their earlier decision to bail out the group, South Korea's eighth-biggest industrial conglomerate.
South Korean banks formed a voluntary committee in April to prevent major companies from going bankrupt by keeping credit lines open and offering emergency loans.
